analysis:
Examined four changed files.

(1) scripts/ci-tested-tree.py adds `ci-tested-tree-<tree>` records accepted for pushes, with weakened head binding (head 119-124, 144-149). Both findings come from this file. Where records are uploaded is not supplied: the gate/upload job in provider-tests.yml and provider-plan.yml. The next pass should verify:
- how the tree name is computed (HEAD^{tree} of the PR merge ref);
- whether records are uploaded when the tests job is skipped (PR without run-ci);
- whether any release workflow (staging from a master push) depends on CI success.

(2) scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py:112-121 now allows a workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev to publish a dev release. It requires RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, a verified commit on dev ancestry, and source == the current dev head. This is stricter than a dev push (which tolerates dev having moved on). Staging and prod remain gated on master or a tag.

(3) scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh:36-43 mirrors this: a dev dispatch forces dev_push=true, validation_only=false and clears the version override, so it cannot select prod or staging. Who may dispatch equals who may push (write access); no regression identified. Whether the Python source verification step runs before signing on the dispatch path is not visible here.

(4) scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py records several workflow changes:
- PR macOS tests are opt-in via the run-ci/run-gpu-ci labels, and an unlabel job removes the label.
- PRs into master now use diff filtering.
- The cluster_gpu gate is added and the hourly dev job is removed.
- Concurrency groups change.

The workflow YAML itself was not supplied. Label-triggered runs from the `labeled` type and the unlabel job's token permissions need review.

findings.detail:
In head scripts/ci-tested-tree.py:144-146, a tree record (record_head is None) passes `head_ok` for any run whose head_sha is a well-formed SHA. Lines 122 and 124 also accept the record from either `pull_request` or `push` events. The base design bound each record to its own change by requiring head_sha == record_head. That binding is why the base docstring (line 31-32) said a record of one change could not stand in for another.

The artifact name is chosen by whatever workflow content ran. A same-repository PR can edit its own copy of the workflow (the docstring at lines 33-34 admits records are only as trustworthy as the workflow at that head). Such a PR could upload `ci-tested-tree-<T>-p1c1m1` for an arbitrary future tree T without running tests. Path equality (line 148) does not check workflow content. When a later squash or merge push to master produces tree T (lines 121-124), it skips every test.

Before this change, a forged record could only match a push whose parents were that PR's own base and head.

Fix options:
- Bind tree records to a run whose head commit's tree equals T. For example, fetch `git/commits/<run.head_sha>` and compare the tree, or use the PR merge-commit tree.
- Alternatively, accept tree records only from push runs on protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-only CI records accept any same-workflow run regardless of head, so a forged record can skip tests for an unrelated change

findings.detail:
Record flags (head ci-tested-tree.py:83-84, 91-92) encode only provider, cluster and mimo_audio, not cluster_gpu. The updated test at scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py hunk @@ -377 shows how the GPU lane is gated:
- A pull_request without the run-gpu-ci label runs cluster with cluster_gpu=false.
- A master push with skip=false runs cluster_gpu=true.
- A master push with skip=true runs cluster_gpu=false.

With the new tree candidate (ci-tested-tree.py:122-124), a run-ci-labeled PR into master can upload a c1 tree record without any GPU testing. A squash merge that yields the same tree then matches that record and skips the master push, so the GPU cluster lane never runs on the release line.

Fix: include cluster_gpu in record flags, or refuse tree records from runs that did not run the GPU lane when the current run would.
findings.title: Tree record reuse lets a master push skip GPU cluster tests that it would otherwise run
